arxiv-2008-08473.title: Cross-Domain Identification for Thermal-to-Visible Face Recognition
arxiv-2008-08473.creator: Cedric Nimpa Fondje, Shuowen Hu, Nathaniel J. Short, Benjamin S. Riggan, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, 1400 R St, Lincoln, NE 68588 CCDC Army Research Laboratory, 2800 Powder Mill Rd., Adelphi, MD 20783 Booz Allen Hamilton, 8283 Grennsboro Dr., McLean, VA 22102, Corresponding authors: cedricnimpa@
arxiv-2008-08473.description: Abstract Recent advances in domain adaptation, especially those applied to heterogeneous facial recognition, typically rely upon restrictive Euclidean loss functions (e.g., L 2 L_{2} norm) which perform best when images from two different domains (e.g., visible and thermal) are co-registered and temporally synchronized.

arxiv-2204-10346.title: Constraining Energy-dependent emissivity profiles of AGN inflows 2022 Constraining Energy-dependent emissivity profiles of AGN inflows – References
arxiv-2204-10346.creator: Dominic I. Ashton, & Matthew J. Middleton
arxiv-2204-10346.description: Abstract The emissivity of the accretion flow is a key parameter affecting the shape of both the energy and variability power spectrum of AGN. We explore the energy-dependence of the power spectrum for five AGN, across the XMM-Newton bandpass, and across the 0.01-1 mHz frequency range, finding a ubiquitous flattening of the power spectrum towards higher energies.

arxiv-2208-12032.title: How (and Why) to Think that the Brain is Literally a Computer forthcoming in Frontiers in Computer Science, Section: Theoretical Computer Science . (doi: 10.3389/fcomp.2022.970396 )
arxiv-2208-12032.creator: Corey J. Maley
arxiv-2208-12032.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Corey J. Maley. The relationship between brains and computers is often taken to be merely metaphorical. However, genuine computational systems can be implemented in virtually any media; thus, one can take seriously the view that brains literally compute. But without empirical criteria for what makes a physical system genuinely a computational one, computation remains a matter of perspective, especially for natural systems (e.g., brains) that were not explicitly designed and engineered to be computers.

arxiv-2303-06075.title: Long-tailed Classification from a Bayesian-decision-theory Perspective
arxiv-2303-06075.creator: Bolian Li, Ruqi Zhang
arxiv-2303-06075.description: Abstract Long-tailed classification poses a challenge due to its heavy imbalance in class probabilities and tail-sensitivity risks with asymmetric misprediction costs. Recent attempts have used re-balancing loss and ensemble methods, but they are largely heuristic and depend heavily on empirical results, lacking theoretical explanation. Furthermore, existing methods overlook the decision loss, which characterizes different costs associated with tailed classes.

arxiv-2408-12254.title: A Language-agnostic Model of Child Language Acquisition
arxiv-2408-12254.creator: Louis Mahon, Omri Abend, Uri Berger, katherine Demuth, Mark Johnson, Mark Steedman
arxiv-2408-12254.description: Abstract This work reimplements a recent semantic bootstrapping cla ( cla ) model, which was originally designed for English, and trains it to learn a new language: Hebrew. The model learns from pairs of utterances and logical forms as meaning representations, and acquires both syntax and word meanings simultaneously.

arxiv-2502-09455.title: Recoil corrections with finite nuclear size in hydrogenic systems
arxiv-2502-09455.creator: Krzysztof Pachucki, Vojtěch Patkóš, Vladimir A. Yerokhin
arxiv-2502-09455.description: Abstract Formulas for the combined nuclear-recoil and finite-nuclear-size effects of order ( Z ​ α ) 5 (Z\alpha)^{5} and ( Z ​ α ) 6 (Z\alpha)^{6} are derived without any expansion in the nuclear-charge radius r C r_{C} , making them applicable to both electronic and muonic atoms.

arxiv-2505-19116.title: Controlling Language Confusion in Multilingual LLMs
arxiv-2505-19116.creator: Nahyun Lee, Yeongseo Woo, Hyunwoo Ko, Guijin Son, Chungang University, OneLineAI, MODULABS
arxiv-2505-19116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nahyun Lee, Yeongseo Woo, Hyunwoo Ko, Guijin Son, Chungang University, OneLineAI, MODULABS. Large language models often suffer from language confusion, a phenomenon in which responses are partially or entirely generated in unintended languages. This critically degrades the user experience, especially in low-resource settings. We hypothesize that this issue stems from limitations in conventional fine-tuning objectives, such as supervised learning, which optimize the likelihood of correct tokens without explicitly penalizing undesired outputs such as cross-lingual mixing.

pmc-10512819.title: Serum amyloid A and risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmc-10512819.creator: Li Li, Hongli Liu, Qinglin Zhang, Hao Jin, Hui Tao, Rong Zhu, Zhongwei Zhou
pmc-10512819.description: BackgroundsThe available literature on the correlation between serum amyloid A (SAA) and prognosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited, and the findings from existing studies are inconclusive. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the available evidence regarding the link between SAA and risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in CKD patients.

pmc-11495225.title: Left Anterior Minithoracotomy for Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Adults
pmc-11495225.creator: Alisson Parrilha Toschi, Rodolfo F. Gomes, Renato B. Pope, Mateus B. Bueno, Cézar Suchard, Isaias Cidral, Robinson Poffo
pmc-11495225.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Surgical interventions on the pulmonary valve in adults have been increasing over the years, as patients with congenital heart diseases are experiencing extended lifespans. Reoperations involving multiple sternotomies exhibit elevated morbidity and mortality rates. With nearly two decades of experience in minimally invasive video-assisted mitral valve surgery, we have chosen the left anterior minithoracotomy approach for addressing the pulmonary valve and right ventricular outflow tract in adult patients.

pmc-11506680.title: Comparative Value of CRP and FCP for Endoscopic and Histologic Remissions in Ulcerative Colitis
pmc-11506680.creator: Oguz Kagan Bakkaloglu, Gozde Sen, Nuray Kepil, Tugce Eskazan, Enes Ali Kurt, Ugur Onal, Selcuk Candan, Melek Balamir, Ibrahim Hatemi, Yusuf Erzin, Aykut Ferhat Celik, Antonio Facciorusso
pmc-11506680.description: Aim: We have previously shown that CRP < 2.9 mg/L is a better predictor of endoscopic remission (ER) than CRP < 5 mg/L in ulcerative colitis (UC). Here, we prospectively evaluate CRP and FCP cut-offs and compare them in predicting ER and histological remission (HR) in UC. Method: One hundred thirty-five steroid-free UC patients were evaluated prospectively.

pmc-11532513.title: A Global Decomposition Analysis of the Effect of Population Aging on Disability-Adjusted Life Years Associated with Cardiovascular Disease — 204 Countries and Territories, 1990–2021
pmc-11532513.creator: Na Sun, Xiaocan Jia, Xuezhong Shi, Feng Jiang, Chaojun Yang, Yongli Yang
pmc-11532513.description: What is already known about this topic?The influence of population aging on the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) is acknowledged, yet the magnitude of this impact remains unclear.What is added by this report?This research quantified the influence of population aging on CVD DALYs from 1990 to 2021 through decomposition analysis.

pmc-12550972.title: Can We Replicate the Most Demanding Periods of Official Football Matches in Large-Sided Training Games?
pmc-12550972.creator: David Casamichana, Iñaki Ulloa, Oier Agirrezabalaga, Ibon Etxeazarra, José Manuel González de Suso, Alfonso Azurza, Bixen Calzon, Jon Mikel Arrieta, Iñigo Sasiain, Jon Ollora, Eider Barba, Beñat Erkizia, Aitor Lazkano, Filipe Manuel Clemente, Julen Castellano, Spyridon Plakias
pmc-12550972.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objective: This study aimed to compare the external load demands of large-sided games, with and without regulatory interruptions, to the average (FOOTmatch) and most demanding scenarios (MDSmatch) observed in official football matches, taking into account players’ pitch positions. Methods: Large-sided training games were implemented with regulatory interruptions (FOOTtask) and without interruptions (MURDtask), during which a coach continuously introduced new balls to maximise effective playing time.

pmc-12619497.title: Diagnostic performance of 1-hour plasma glucose and glucose curve shape during oral glucose tolerance test: a cross-sectional study in a Brazilian cohort
pmc-12619497.creator: João Pedro F C Castro, Delanie B Macedo, Rejane A Magalhaes, Cecília M M Figueirêdo, Rachel Petrola, Milena G Teles
pmc-12619497.description: BackgroundThe 1-h plasma glucose (1-h PG) during oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) may enhance early dysglycemia detection compared with conventional markers. Distinct glucose curve morphologies correlate with glycemic profiles, insulin sensitivity, and β-cell function. We aimed to compare 1-h PG diagnostic performance with conventional methods and explored glucose curve morphology prevalence in a Brazilian population.

pmc-12862116.title: Lived Experience of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Survivors: A Phenomenological Study
pmc-12862116.creator: Meng Zhang, Anqi Sun, Anqi Yu, Juan Deng, Yi Wang, Xiao Cheng, Jie Xiong
pmc-12862116.description: BackgroundExtracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a vital extracorporeal life support for acute cardiopulmonary failure, serving as a critical lifesaving measure widely utilised during the COVID‐19 pandemic. Despite the enhancement of survival rates and the extension of its utilisation, ECMO survivors face complications and post‐discharge challenges.

pmc-12980106.title: Return to work after myocardial infarction: A systematic review
pmc-12980106.creator: Tais Santana Barbosa, Natasha Cordeiro dos Santos, Millena Pereira Costa, Roque Aras Junior
pmc-12980106.description: The majority of people experiencing Myocardial Infarction are of working age, which may result in prolonged work disability. This study seeks to consolidate the available evidence regarding the return to work for individuals following a Myocardial Infarction, while also examining its correlation with disease severity, job engagement, and duration of hospitalization. This research is a systematic review.

pmc-13212642.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identifies a Pivotal Role of SPHK1+ Macrophage-Driven Inflammation in Mechanism of Aortic Dissection and Highlights SPHK1 as a Therapeutic Target
pmc-13212642.creator: Dianjun Tang, Yanshuo Han, Han Jiang, Jamol Uzokov, Fandong Li, Zhong Wang, Mario D’Oria, Philipp Erhart, Dittmar Boeckler, Yu Lun, Jian Zhang
pmc-13212642.description: Macrophages are a key heterogeneous cell population involved in the pathogenesis and progression of acute aortic dissection (AD), though their mechanisms remain unclear. This study aims to identify the gene driving inflammatory damage in acute AD within a specific macrophage subcluster, highlighting potential therapeutic targets.

pmc-13214356.title: Application of reinforced U-shaped suture technique in laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy: an analysis of 165 consecutive cases
pmc-13214356.creator: Yuanjie Sun, Tingshuo Zhao, Yutao Wu, Zhigang Wei, Jie Yu
pmc-13214356.description: ObjectivePostoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) remains a major postoperative complication of laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy (LDP) that severely impacts surgical safety and patient prognosis. This study was designed to investigate the clinical efficacy of the reinforced U-shaped suture technique in reducing the incidence of POPF after LDP, and to identify independent risk factors for POPF to provide evidence-based references for clinical practice.

pmc-13573840.title: USP18 Serves as a Key Mediator of cGAS‐STING for Cardiac Aging in Diabetes
pmc-13573840.creator: Xunxi Deng, Zhiyi Yin, Shi Tai, Hejun Jiang, Yuying Zhou, Yongjun Wang, Liyao Fu
pmc-13573840.description: Diabetes accelerates cardiac aging, but the molecular mechanisms that link metabolic stress to myocardial senescence remain insufficiently defined. This study investigated factors driving diabetes‐associated cardiac aging with a focus on the role of USP18. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) was induced in mice using a high‐fat diet combined with streptozotocin.
